numerical_failure.observed_behavior: DataFrame.idxmax/idxmin on a nullable UInt64 column with NA returned the wrong row, because the +/-inf sentinel fill was an np.int64 scalar that under NEP 50 promoted the uint64 array to float64 in np.where, losing precision above 2**53. Separately, nanargmin/nanargmax could return a masked (NA) position that precedes real values when real values tie the dtype-extreme fill; e.g. an all-zero uint64 column with a leading NA. Also idxmax on a float column containing only -inf and NaN returned the NaN row (idxmin with +inf likewise).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Unsigned dtypes use a uint64 sentinel (u8max for the min-fill, 0 for the max-fill) so the array stays unsigned and no precision is lost. When a winner lands on a masked position (every unmasked value ties the fill), the first unmasked position is returned instead.
trigger_conditions: nullable UInt64 column containing NA with values above 2**53 passed to DataFrame.idxmax/idxmin
uint64 masked array with values tying the max-fill of 0, e.g. all-zero column with a leading NA
float column containing only -inf and NaN passed to idxmax (or +inf and NaN to idxmin)
nullable integer columns whose values all equal the dtype extreme (i8min/i8max/u8max) passed to DataFrame.idxmax/idxmin

numerical_characteristics.precision: Values above 2**53 lose precision when a uint64 array is promoted to float64 via the int64 sentinel in np.where under NEP 50; the fix keeps the sentinel as uint64. The tie path is a separate failure with no precision loss, triggered by fill values equal to the dtype extremes (uint64 0 and 2**64-1, int64 min and max, float -inf and +inf).
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Values above 2**53 (precision loss). Values above 2**63 (test values 2**63+1 to 2**63+3; i8max cannot bracket them). Full uint64 range bracketed by u8max and 0.
category_specific_evidence: nanops._get_fill_value changed the +/-inf sentinel from a Python int to np.int64, which promotes uint64 masked arrays to float64 in np.where under NEP 50, losing precision above 2**53 and returning the wrong idxmax/idxmin row (GH#64478).
The fix returns np.uint64(lib.u8max) for the +inf fill and np.uint64(0) for the -inf fill on unsigned dtypes.
test_nanargminmax_uint64_with_mask uses values 2**63+1..2**63+3 plus 0 with a masked position at index 0 or 3, and checks nanargmax, nanargmin, nanmax and nanmin against an unmasked reference.
test_idxminmax_uint64_with_na uses UInt64 values 2**63+1..2**63+3 with pd.NA and expects idxmax [2] and idxmin [0].

Sentinel-tie bug: NA fill equals the dtype extremes, so real values can tie the fill. The uint64 max-fill of 0 makes an all-zero column with a leading NA common. The fix returns the first unmasked position when the winner lands on a masked position.
test_nanargminmax_uint64_na_tie covers uint64 tie values 0 and 2**64-1 with a leading NA; test_nanargminmax_int64_na_tie covers int64 min and max.
Float tie tests: nanargmax([nan,-inf,-inf]) == 1 and nanargmin([nan,inf,inf]) == 1; test_idxminmax_float_inf_tie checks DataFrame and Series idxmax/idxmin.
test_idxminmax_uint64_all_zero_with_na builds a UInt64 column [NA,0,0] and expects idxmax and idxmin both [1].

Changelog v3.1.0 entry: idxmax/idxmin returned the label of a missing-value row when all non-missing values equal the dtype minimum (idxmax) or maximum (idxmin), e.g. a float column with only -inf and NaN (:issue:64478).
